common_causes.label: O2 sensor contaminated (silicone, lead, fuel additives)
O2 sensor aged beyond service life
Exhaust leak upstream of O2 sensor

characteristic_signatures.o2_sensor_contamination: O2 voltage stuck or railed; no switching; response time much slower than spec; often from silicone or leaded fuel exposure.
characteristic_signatures.o2_sensor_aging: O2 switching rate degrades gradually over time; voltage peaks may not reach full lean/rich extremes.
characteristic_signatures.o2_heater_fault: O2 readings slow to respond when cold; improves as sensor heats up; heater circuit DTC may also be present.
characteristic_signatures.exhaust_leak: O2 reads lean near leak due to ambient air ingress; may improve under load when exhaust pressure rises.
characteristic_signatures.wiring_fault: Intermittent O2 signal; may show noise or dropouts correlated with harness movement.

available_tests.label: Disconnect O2, check if trims reset in open-loop
Swap O2 sensor with known-good unit
